change.author: Julius Marminge

findings.title: Anyone redirected to the hosted page who can't reach the environment through T3 Connect has no way to the code page
findings.body: `authorize` now sends every non-link sign-in on the linked tunnel host to the hosted `/approve-agent` page (`apps/server/src/auth/mcpOAuthHttp.ts:127-135`). The 'Use a sign-in code instead' link only renders once `environment` is set (line 159), and `environment` is set only after a call succeeds in `connectTransport` (lines 50-53). If the visitor signs in to a T3 Connect account that does not own the environment, or the relay or `authorizeDpopHttp` fails, `runConnectMcpApproval` returns `ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError`, `environment` stays null, and the page shows 'This sign-in cannot continue … Close this page' with only 'Use another account'. Before this change the environment's own `/connect-agent` page always offered the code field. A person who holds a pairing code but no T3 Connect account for that environment (for example a collaborator on the tunnel URL) is now stuck, and the server cannot tell them apart before redirecting. Give the hosted page a fallback to the environment's own page that does not depend on a successful relay call. The server could, for example, only redirect when it can trust the visitor is the owner, or the hosted page could keep a link that is not gated on `environment`.

findings.title: Does a T3 Connect owner session always hold `access:write` and `orchestration:read`?
findings.body: The comment says the owner's session can always approve, and a details answer without `csrfToken` is treated as a stale credential. But `approvingSession` (`apps/server/src/auth/McpOAuth.ts:410-422`) returns no `csrfToken` unless the session holds both `access:write` and `orchestration:read`, and it swallows every auth error into `undefined`. If a relay-issued session can lack either scope, such as a reduced-scope or managed-policy account, the client retries once and then fails with 'rejected the renewed session authorization'. `mapError` at line 109 then shows 'Could not reach that environment through T3 Connect with this account', which is the wrong diagnosis. Please confirm the scopes the relay DPoP session carries, or give the missing-scope case its own message.

findings.title: A second hosted-app URL config that differs from `hostedAppUrlConfig` only by default
findings.body: `agentApprovalAppUrlConfig` reads the same `T3CODE_HOSTED_APP_URL` as `hostedAppUrlConfig` and only changes the default for nightly builds. The environment now has two answers to 'where is the hosted app', and the other consumers of `hostedAppUrlConfig` still point a nightly build at `app.t3.codes`. Consider giving the nightly default to `hostedAppUrlConfig` itself, or documenting why only agent approvals should follow the channel. Also confirm `https://nightly.app.t3.codes` serves `/approve-agent` before this ships, because a wrong host sends every nightly tunnel sign-in to a dead page.

findings.title: Docs and page hint send users to a code source that no longer mints codes on current environments
findings.body: The fallback described here ("Use a sign-in code instead" → the environment's own page) asks for "a code from Use T3 Code in another app (MCP)". On an environment with `mcpHostedApproval` (set for every current server, apps/server/src/environment/ServerEnvironment.ts:292) that wizard now shows no `ApprovalCode` (UseInAnotherAppDialog.tsx:566-571), and the doc's own line 19-22 says only older environments get a code from it. The same stale hint is in the code field on the environment's page (ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:319), and the sentence at line 72 about a code carrying the picked level. Reword to name only Settings → Sharing & access and `t3 auth pairing create` for current environments, and say the wizard code is for older ones.

findings.title: Hosted mode skips the managed-policy and permission gate that the Access step enforced
findings.body: `useGrantableLevels` (line 209-231) blocked every level when the managed policy denies `remoteClients` or the device lacks Manage access, so Next was disabled at step 1. With `hostedApproval` the Access step is skipped and `levels` is not consulted, so the wizard goes on to the Connect step regardless. The comment at line 214 says the server refuses codes in that case, but I found no `remoteClients` check in apps/server/src, so I could not confirm the server refuses a browser-session approval for the same policy. Does the hosted approval path enforce the remote-clients denial server-side? If not, the wizard should still show the denial.

contracts.action: Hosted app approves an agent sign-in on a T3 Connect environment with the owner's DPoP session, with no code
contracts.equivalent_path: The environment's own /connect-agent page: `primaryTransport` in apps/web/src/components/auth/ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:108-115, authenticated by the browser cookie or a pairing code, which `McpOAuth.approve` checks for a CSRF token at McpOAuth.ts:471-480.
contracts.before_after: Before: the hosted app minted a one-use approval code and returned it in the fragment to the environment's page, which then used it. After: the hosted app calls `/oauth/mcp/approval` and `/oauth/mcp/decision` directly with `Authorization: DPoP` and a proof. The server's `approvingSession` now uses `authenticateHttpRequest` instead of the cookie-only `authenticateBrowserSession`, and derives the CSRF token from the session id. Scope and CSRF checks are unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: Consent screen on the hosted page with the environment label, or an error message or redirect to the agent.
contracts.failure_mode: Relay or authorization failure becomes ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError, shown as 'Could not reach…'. A rejected credential is detected only through a missing csrfToken, because approvingSession swallows auth errors. The decision call has no equivalent check, so a renewed token with a different session id gives a CSRF mismatch and 'enter a pairing code', which this page has no field for. Token lifetime is about an hour, so this is rare.

contracts.action: Bound on the whole hosted approval call
contracts.equivalent_path: The other `executeAuthenticatedEnvironmentHttpRequest` callers, for example mintPairingCredential in peerPairingCode.ts.
contracts.before_after: `authorizeDpopHttp` at line 64 runs outside the 10s `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`. Inside, `executeEnvironmentRequest` wraps the credential renewal, the request and one retry in a single `timeoutOrElse` of 10s (environmentHttpAuth.ts:260-271). The token exchange itself is capped at DPOP_AUTHORIZATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 30s (service.ts:445-454, constant at :102).
contracts.visible_effect: Worst case about 30s of spinner for the first authorization plus 10s for the request, then the 'Could not reach' message. The Approve button shows its pending state meanwhile.
contracts.failure_mode: Timeout becomes ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError, shown to the user and retryable. A timed-out token renewal is not cancelled for other callers, because it runs in a forked scope.

contracts.action: `headers: OptionalBearerHeaders` added to the approval and decision endpoints
contracts.equivalent_path: The other endpoints in the same file that already use OptionalBearerHeaders (lines 563-966).
contracts.before_after: The generated client now requires `headers` on `mcpOAuth.approval` and `mcpOAuth.decision`. Callers: ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:110 and :113, PeerLinks.ts:312, and the new connectMcpApproval.ts, which passes headers built from the signer. The server reads the Authorization and DPoP headers in `authenticateRequest`.
contracts.visible_effect: Typecheck breaks any caller that omits `headers`. None remain in the repository.
contracts.failure_mode: If a call passes `headers: {}`, the server falls back to the cookie, the same as before.

contracts.action: Server redirects an agent sign-in on the linked tunnel host to the hosted /approve-agent page
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous flow: the environment's /connect-agent page returned `connectSignIn` in the approval details, and the user chose to go to the hosted app.
contracts.before_after: Before, the user always landed on /connect-agent and could choose. Now the redirect is automatic for non-link clients when linkState is linked, not revoked, and the tunnel hostname equals the issuer host. The hosted page decodes the query with `readAuthorizationRequest`, whose schema fields are all optional, so the extra `environment` param is ignored. It reads `environment` itself.
contracts.visible_effect: The user leaves the environment's origin and must sign in to T3 Connect. A cookie session on the tunnel no longer gives one-click approval.
contracts.failure_mode: `linkState` errors fall back to /connect-agent through `orElseSucceed(Option.none)`. A non-owner has no code fallback (see the finding on ApproveAgentSurface.tsx:159).

contracts.equivalent_path: `mcpApprovalCodes` at ServerEnvironment.ts:291, the sibling optional capability flag.
contracts.before_after: The server always advertises true. The only reader is UseInAnotherAppDialog.tsx:126, which drops the Access step when it is true. A server without the flag leaves it undefined and the dialog keeps the code flow.
contracts.visible_effect: The wizard has two steps instead of three on supporting environments.
contracts.failure_mode: A flag advertised by the server does not guarantee that the hosted app serving /approve-agent for the configured URL has the new page. That depends on the hosted app's deployment, which is not visible from this repository.

contracts.action: `agentRedirectUrl` gates the post-decision redirect to https or loopback http
contracts.equivalent_path: Server-side redirect URI check in McpOAuth.ts:108-111, which allows https or http on LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES.
contracts.before_after: The client check uses the shared `isLoopbackHost`, and the server uses a three-entry set of localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1]. The server cannot register any other scheme, so the new client check refuses nothing a valid registration produces.
contracts.visible_effect: An unexpected scheme shows 'The environment returned an address this page will not open.'

contracts.action: McpConsent loads the sign-in request and sends the decision through a transport (primary or T3 Connect)
contracts.equivalent_path: Old ConnectAgentSurface called runApproval directly and handled a T3 Connect return via sessionStorage nonce; new primaryTransport sends the same approval/decision calls with `headers: {}`.
contracts.before_after: Before: load, then optional auto-submit on Connect return; after: load only, Approve is gated by `armed` (700 ms after ready and after each focus/visibility change). Endpoints accept `headers` (OptionalBearerHeaders) so `headers: {}` is valid.
contracts.visible_effect: Loading spinner, then consent screen; Approve is disabled for 700 ms and re-disabled on window focus; errors shown in an Alert.
contracts.failure_mode: Load error or non-redirect decision answer sets an invalid/error state and re-enables the buttons; cancelled flag ignores stale loads.

contracts.action: Window is redirected to the address returned by approval/decision via agentRedirectUrl
contracts.equivalent_path: Old code called window.location.replace(answer.url) unchecked; the server only registers https or loopback-http redirect URIs.
contracts.before_after: New client check (https, or http on a loopback host) matches the server's own rule, so legitimate redirects still pass; javascript:/data: are refused and shown as an error.
contracts.visible_effect: Agent callback opens after approval; an unsafe address shows 'The environment returned an address this page will not open.'
contracts.failure_mode: A refused redirect leaves the page with pending cleared and an error message; no silent failure.

contracts.action: Wizard drops the Access step and the code when the environment reports mcpHostedApproval
contracts.equivalent_path: Server redirects /authorize to the hosted /approve-agent only when the linked tunnel hostname equals the issuer host and the client is not a peer link; otherwise to the environment's /connect-agent which needs a code.
contracts.before_after: The capability is true on every current server; the wizard URL comes from the T3 Connect tunnel gate, so the hosted redirect applies for that URL. Wizard no longer mints a code in that mode.
contracts.visible_effect: Two steps (App, Connect) and a note to choose the level on the sign-in page.
contracts.failure_mode: If the page opens on the environment instead (fallback link), the user has no wizard-minted code; see docs finding. Managed-policy denial is no longer shown in the wizard (question finding).
contracts.open_question: Does the server enforce the managed remote-clients policy for browser-session/hosted approvals?

contracts.action: runConnectMcpApproval runs the client-runtime Connect approval command
contracts.equivalent_path: mintMcpApprovalCodeOn in apps/web/src/state/peerPairingCode.ts:35-43 wraps a command the same way.
contracts.before_after: Same run + squashAtomCommandFailure shape as the sibling; failures become Result.fail, which ApproveAgentSurface maps to a user message.
contracts.visible_effect: Consent page for T3 Connect environments loads and decides with the account's session.
contracts.failure_mode: Rejection or timeout (10 s in the command) becomes ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError and an error message on the page.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** The server and client-runtime changes are consistent: the HTTP contract, the `approvingSession` swap, the retry and timeout handling, and the redirect to the hosted page all line up with what the other side reads. One real problem: a visitor redirected to the hosted page whose T3 Connect account can't reach the environment gets an error screen with no link back to the code page, because that link only appears after a successful relay call. Two smaller items: whether a relay-issued owner session always holds `access:write` and `orchestration:read`, and the duplicated hosted-app URL config. I read the tests and removed code and found nothing wrong. I did not read `pr.json`, so I did not check the PR description against the code.

**Batch 2 of 2.** The consent screen is now one `McpConsent` component fed by a transport, with a 700 ms arming delay on Approve and a redirect allow-list. The allow-list matches the server's own https/loopback rule, and the new test covers it. I found no defects in the code itself. Two points to settle. First, the docs and the code-field hint on the environment's page still tell users to get a code from the wizard, which no longer mints one on current environments. Second, in hosted mode the wizard skips the managed-policy check, and I could not confirm the server enforces it for browser-session approvals.
